outcomeNote: A mishna stating four rulings; no question is raised and no parties interact within the unit.

segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁיָּצְאָה לֵיהָרֵג, אֵין מַמְתִּינִין לָהּ עַד שֶׁתֵּלֵד. הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁיָּשְׁבָה עַל הַמַּשְׁבֵּר, מַמְתִּינִין לָהּ עַד שֶׁתֵּלֵד. הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁנֶּהֶרְגָה, נֶהֱנִין בִּשְׂעָרָהּ. בְּהֵמָה שֶׁנֶּהֶרְגָה, אֲסוּרָה בַּהֲנָאָה.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» In the case of a pregnant «woman who is taken» by the court «to be executed,» the court «does not wait to» execute «her until she gives birth.» Rather, she is killed immediately. But with regard to «a woman» taken to be executed «who sat on the travailing chair [hamashber]» in the throes of labor, the court «waits to» execute «her until she gives birth.» In the case of «a woman who was killed» through court-imposed capital punishment, «one may derive benefit from her hair.» But in the case of «an animal that was killed» through court-imposed execution, e.g., for goring a person, «deriving benefit» from the animal «is prohibited.»

moves.summary: A pregnant woman taken out to be executed is killed at once; the court does not wait for her to give birth.
Once she has sat on the birthing stool the court does wait until she gives birth.
One may derive benefit from the hair of a woman put to death by the court.
An animal put to death by the court is forbidden for benefit — the counterpart to the previous clause.
